subject: Urban Planning
title: ADUs: Legalizing Backyard Homes
description: A quick win: understand ADUs: Legalizing Backyard Homes.

hook.text: California legalized granny flats statewide in 2017. Homeowners can now build small homes in their backyards.

buildup.text: Accessory dwelling units add density gently — no towers, no demolition, just small homes behind existing ones.

discovery.text: ADUs let homeowners house aging parents, earn rental income, or provide affordable units — all on one lot.

twist.text: Permit costs and construction expenses still price out many homeowners. A backyard unit can cost $200,000.

climax.text: Prefab ADU companies now ship factory-built units that install in weeks for under $100,000.

punchline.text: A tiny house in the backyard. The gentlest density there is.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of accessory dwelling units for increasing housing supply?
options: They replace aging homes with modern apartments
They add density gently within existing neighborhoods without demolition
They allow commercial businesses to operate in residential areas
